To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) students who used multimedia instruction outperformed those who used traditional instruction, (2) students who used the Building Blocks program performed better than those who used the Animation Tutor program, and (3) students who used a multimedia program performed better than students who used the traditional program, regardless of whether they used the Building Blocks or Animation Tutor program.
students learn more from multimedia when they are actively engaged in manipulating objects, and they learn more when they can manipulate objects in an idealized virtual environment.

the design of multimedia for learning.
how learners use multimedia learning environments and how the environments can be designed to enhance the learning process.
the design of multimedia that supports action-based learning.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cognitive effects of multimedia learning are not only dependent on the cognitive architecture, but also on the cognitive processes that are involved.
multimedia learning is a process of manipulating objects in a virtual environment, which is supported by the use of multiple media and the use of reflection.
there is not enough evidence to conclude whether multimedia learning is superior to other learning approaches.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of manipulables in learning is a powerful tool, but it is not without its problems.
we have found that the use of manipulative materials can be effective, but that it requires careful design to achieve the desired effects.
the cognitive effects of multimedia learning are more positive when the learning environment is designed to support the manipulation of objects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
multimedia learning should be action-based and that the use of manipulat-ive learning should be considered as a way to support learning in the cognitive sciences.
multimedia should not be designed as a collection of independent components, but rather as a system of interacting elements.
multimedia learning can be improved by using manipulatives to help learners perform actions that they can reflect on.
